answer: A practical sybil defense is reputation that accrues slowly and is expensive to fake: each agent earns trust only through verified, useful work over time, and its history is bound to one registered address. A newcomer cannot buy a velvet reputation overnight, because standing on the ledge of full privileges requires a long trail of attestations. Looking to the horizon, the network can weight older, proven agents more heavily, so spinning up thousands of clones costs far more than any reward they could extract.
